system.name: Hogarel home-policy assistant
system.purpose: Answers policyholders' questions about the Hogar Completo home policy on the Hogarel website: cover, exclusions, excesses, claims, payments and changes.

findings.title: Incomplete answers
findings.observation: 8 of 46 answers were right as far as they went but left out key facts.
findings.cause_hypothesis: Likely cause: knowledge gap (4), wrong source (4).
findings.recommendation: Make sure the complete information (conditions, limits, alternatives) is available to the assistant and that answers are not cut short.

findings.title: Answers with wrong information
findings.observation: 6 of 46 answers stated information that does not match your documentation.
findings.cause_hypothesis: Likely cause: invented answer (4), outdated document (2).
findings.recommendation: Correct or update the content the assistant relies on for these topics, then re-run the same tests to confirm the fix.

findings.title: Answers that contradict your documentation
findings.observation: 2 of 46 answers contradicted what your documentation says.
findings.recommendation: Find the outdated or conflicting source the assistant used, remove or correct it, and re-run the same tests.

findings.title: The assistant did not answer
findings.observation: 5 of 46 questions got no usable answer: the assistant deflected, asked to rephrase or offered options without answering.
findings.recommendation: Check that these topics are covered by the assistant's knowledge and that its fallback does not trigger on clear, in-scope questions.

results.title: Burst pipe under the sink
results.input: A pipe burst under my kitchen sink and flooded the floor. Is that covered?
results.output: Yes, that's covered. Sudden and accidental water leaks from pipes are included in your Hogar Completo policy, both for damage to the home and to your belongings. We also pay to repair the pipe that caused the leak, up to €600. You can report the claim from the app.
results.rationale: Confirms cover for a sudden escape of water and gives the €600 limit for repairing the pipe, as in article 2.1.
results.label: correct
results.expected: Yes. A sudden, accidental escape of water is covered for the building and contents, including repairing the pipe that caused it, up to €600.

key_facts.fact: A sudden escape of water is covered

source_excerpts.title: Hogar Completo general conditions (2026 edition)
source_excerpts.excerpt: 2.1 Water damage. We cover damage to the building and contents caused by a sudden and accidental escape of water from pipes, tanks, heating systems or connected appliances. We also pay to repair the pipe that caused the damage, up to €600, and to locate a hidden leak, up to €300 per claim, even when it has not yet caused damage.

results.title: Hidden leak with no damage yet
results.input: My water bill has doubled and I think there's a hidden leak, but there's no visible damage yet. Do you pay to find it?
results.output: Leak detection is only covered when the leak has already caused damage to your home. If there's no damage, the cost of finding the leak is not covered.
results.rationale: Says leak detection needs existing damage. Article 2.1 covers it up to €300 even when there is no damage yet.
results.label: incorrect
results.expected: Yes. Locating a hidden leak is covered up to €300 per claim, even if it has not caused damage yet.

key_facts.fact: Leak detection is covered without damage

source_excerpts.title: Hogar Completo general conditions (2026 edition)
source_excerpts.excerpt: 2.1 Water damage. We cover damage to the building and contents caused by a sudden and accidental escape of water from pipes, tanks, heating systems or connected appliances. We also pay to repair the pipe that caused the damage, up to €600, and to locate a hidden leak, up to €300 per claim, even when it has not yet caused damage.

contradictions: Says detection needs existing damage; the policy covers it without damage.

results.title: Power surge damaged two appliances
results.input: A power surge fried my TV and the washing machine. The washing machine is 12 years old. What do you pay?
results.output: A power surge is covered under electrical damage, up to €1,500 per claim, and that includes the TV. Because the washing machine is more than 10 years old, it's paid at its actual value, after depreciation, rather than the price of a new one.
results.rationale: Gives the €1,500 limit and correctly applies the actual-value rule for appliances over 10 years old (article 2.5).
results.label: correct
results.expected: Electrical damage from a power surge is covered up to €1,500 per claim. Appliances more than 10 years old, like the washing machine, are paid at their actual value after depreciation.

key_facts.fact: Appliances over 10 years paid at actual value

source_excerpts.title: Hogar Completo general conditions (2026 edition)
source_excerpts.excerpt: 2.5 Electrical damage. Damage to the electrical installation and to appliances caused by a short circuit or power surge is covered up to €1,500 per claim. Appliances more than 10 years old are paid at their actual value, after depreciation.

results.title: Excess for water damage
results.input: How much do I pay myself if I claim for water damage?
results.output: Water-damage claims have an excess of €150 per claim, which is deducted from the amount we pay. Other claims have no excess.
results.rationale: Gives a €150 excess. The 2026 general conditions (article 4) set it at €200; €150 was the amount in the previous edition.
results.label: incorrect
results.expected: Water-damage claims have an excess of €200 per claim.

source_excerpts.title: Hogar Completo general conditions (2026 edition)
source_excerpts.excerpt: 4. Excess. Claims have no excess, except water-damage claims, which have an excess of €200 per claim. The excess also applies to the repair of the pipe that caused the damage.

contradictions: States a €150 excess; article 4 sets €200.

results.title: Excess on a burglary claim
results.input: Is there an excess if I claim for a burglary?
results.output: No, theft claims have no excess. The only excess in your policy applies to water-damage claims.
results.rationale: Correct: article 4 applies an excess only to water damage.
results.label: correct
results.expected: No. Only water-damage claims have an excess; theft claims have none.

source_excerpts.title: Hogar Completo general conditions (2026 edition)
source_excerpts.excerpt: 4. Excess. Claims have no excess, except water-damage claims, which have an excess of €200 per claim. The excess also applies to the repair of the pipe that caused the damage.

results.title: Excess when water damages a neighbour
results.input: Water from my bathroom leaked into the flat below. Do I pay an excess for the neighbour's damage and for mine?
results.output: Both are covered. A €150 excess applies to the claim, and it covers your neighbour's repairs and your own.
results.rationale: Applies a €150 excess to both. The neighbour's damage is paid under liability without an excess, and the water-damage excess is €200 in 2026.
results.label: incorrect
results.expected: The neighbour's damage is paid under family liability with no excess. The damage inside your own home is water damage, with the €200 excess.

source_excerpts.title: Home insurance FAQ (2026)
source_excerpts.excerpt: If water from your home damages a neighbour's flat, the neighbour's damage is paid under family liability, with no excess. Damage inside your own home is paid under water damage, with the €200 excess.

contradictions: Applies an excess to the neighbour's damage, which is paid under liability without one.

results.title: Jewellery stolen in a burglary
results.input: Burglars took my jewellery, about €2,400 worth. How much will you pay?
results.output: Jewellery and watches are covered up to €3,000 per claim, so the full €2,400 would be paid once the claim is accepted. Report the burglary to the police and send us the report with photos or receipts.
results.rationale: Gives the €3,000 limit but leaves out the condition that decides this case: jewellery worth more than €1,500 is covered only if it was in a locked safe. The customer may expect a payment the policy does not guarantee.
results.label: partially_correct
results.expected: Jewellery is covered up to €3,000 per claim, but because it is worth more than €1,500 in total, it is covered only if it was kept in a locked safe.

key_facts.fact: Over €1,500 in total: only if kept in a locked safe

source_excerpts.title: Table of limits and excesses (2026)
source_excerpts.excerpt: Jewellery and watches: up to €3,000 per claim. (1) If the jewellery stolen from the home is worth more than €1,500 in total, it is covered only if it was kept in a locked safe.

results.title: Jewellery kept outside a safe
results.input: I keep my jewellery in a drawer, not a safe. It's worth about €4,000. Is it covered if it's stolen from the house?
results.output: Jewellery is covered up to €3,000 per claim. For valuable items we recommend keeping them in a safe.
results.rationale: Gives the €3,000 limit and mentions a safe only as advice; it does not say that without a safe this jewellery is not covered.
results.label: partially_correct
results.expected: Jewellery is covered up to €3,000 per claim, but jewellery worth more than €1,500 in total is covered only if it was kept in a locked safe, so a theft from the drawer would not be covered.

key_facts.fact: Over €1,500 and not in a safe: not covered

results.output: Theft outside your home is only covered in Spain. For theft abroad, check whether your travel insurance covers it.
results.rationale: Says cover is limited to Spain. Article 2.3 covers theft away from home worldwide, up to €600.
results.label: incorrect

results.rationale: Correctly applies the 45-day exclusion in article 3(d).
results.label: correct
results.expected: No. Theft of contents is not covered when the home has been uninhabited for more than 45 consecutive days.

results.output: No, I'm afraid not. Glass breakage covers windows, glass doors, mirrors and glass-ceramic or induction hobs, but not the screens of phones, tablets, computers or TVs.
results.rationale: States the exclusion for phone screens and what the cover includes (article 2.4).

results.title: Damp and mould from a slow leak
results.input: There's damp and black mould on my bedroom wall from a slow leak inside the wall. Can I claim for the repairs?
results.output: Yes, water damage is covered, including damp and mould caused by leaks. Report it in the app with photos and we'll send an adjuster.
results.rationale: Says damp and mould from a slow leak are covered. Article 3(b) excludes damp, mould and leaks that develop gradually. A customer could start repairs expecting a payment that will be refused.
results.label: incorrect
results.expected: No. Damp, condensation, mould and leaks that develop gradually are excluded (article 3b). A sudden escape of water would be covered; gradual damage is not.

key_facts.fact: Gradual leaks, damp and mould are excluded

results.label: correct

system.name: Hogarel home-policy assistant
system.purpose: Answers policyholders' questions about the Hogar Completo home policy on the Hogarel website: cover, exclusions, excesses, claims, payments and changes.

findings.title: Says damp and gradual leaks are covered
findings.observation: Asked about damp and mould from a slow leak, the assistant said the damage is covered and offered an adjuster. The general conditions exclude damp, condensation, mould and gradual leaks (article 3b).
findings.cause_hypothesis: The assistant appears to generalise from the water-damage cover without retrieving the exclusions article.
findings.recommendation: Add an answer that states the exclusion for damp, condensation, mould and gradual leaks, and require the assistant to cite article 3 whenever it answers about damp.

findings.title: Leaves out the safe condition for jewellery
findings.observation: Both jewellery questions got the €3,000 limit without the condition that decides them: jewellery worth more than €1,500 is covered only in a locked safe. In October one answer said jewellery is covered wherever it is kept.
findings.cause_hypothesis: The condition is a footnote in the table of limits; the answers follow the FAQ summary, which does not include it.
findings.recommendation: Add the safe condition to the FAQ answer on jewellery and index the footnotes of the table of limits as part of each row.

findings.title: Quotes last year's water-damage excess
findings.observation: All three questions about the water-damage excess got last year's amount or a hedge: €150 twice, and "€150 or €200, depending on your policy edition" once. The 2026 conditions set €200, and the neighbour's damage has no excess at all.
findings.cause_hypothesis: The assistant's sources still include the 2025 FAQ, which states a €150 excess.
findings.recommendation: Remove the 2025 FAQ from the assistant's sources and re-run the three water-excess questions.

findings.title: Mixes up cancelling and the right of withdrawal
findings.observation: Asked how to cancel, the assistant described the 14-day right of withdrawal, with a refund for unused days, instead of the one-month notice before renewal. Asked about withdrawal, it gave the 14 days but not what is refunded.
findings.cause_hypothesis: Both rules are in article 7; the answers blend the two paragraphs.
findings.recommendation: Write separate answers for cancelling at renewal and for withdrawing in the first 14 days, each with its own conditions.

findings.title: Leaves payment questions unanswered
findings.observation: Two of five payment questions still get a fallback menu or "I don't have that information": changing the payment schedule and returned direct debits. The September FAQ update fixed the other two.
findings.cause_hypothesis: These topics are not in the assistant's knowledge base; the answers exist in article 6 and in the FAQ.
findings.recommendation: Add article 6 and the payment FAQ to the assistant's sources and re-run the payment questions.

findings.title: New glass answer drops the screen exclusion
findings.observation: Correct in August and September, the answer about a cracked phone screen no longer says that screens are excluded. The customer has to infer it.
findings.cause_hypothesis: The rewritten glass-breakage FAQ lists what is covered but not what is excluded.
findings.recommendation: Restore the exclusion for phone, tablet, computer and TV screens in the glass-breakage answer.

methodology.sampling: A frozen test set of 48 questions written from the five synthetic source documents and used unchanged in all three monthly runs; no question was added or removed after seeing results.
methodology.review_coverage: Every assessed result of the October run is marked as approved by a reviewer. In this example the review is simulated: no real expert reviewed it.
limitations: Synthetic example: the company, its documents, the assistant's answers and the review are invented to show what a report contains.
Likely causes are hypotheses drawn from the evidence; they have not been verified with the system owner.
1 test was flagged as unclear or with a questionable expected answer and excluded from the score until reviewed.
1 answer was not captured reliably from the web app and excluded from the score.

takeaways.text: 35 of 46 assessed answers were correct (76%), up from 54% in August and 65% in September. Seven questions improved since September and two regressed.
The costliest error is a wrong "yes": the assistant says damp and gradual leaks are covered, and the policy excludes them.
Jewellery answers leave out the safe condition, so a customer could expect a payment the policy does not give.
All three answers about the water-damage excess are wrong or hedged because the assistant still uses last year's €150; removing the 2025 FAQ should fix all three.
Two payment questions still get no answer; the September update fixed the other two, so adding article 6 to the sources should close the gap.
